t: The consent herein granted does not extend to paragraph B of article 11 or to paragraphs.!, K, and M of article VI of the compact, or to other provisions of article, VI of the compact which purport to authorize recommendations to, or cooperation with, any foreign or international governments, political subdivisions, agencies or bodies. In carrying out its functions under this Act the Commission shall be solely a consultative and recommendatory agency which will cooperate with the agencies of the United States. It shall furnish to the Congress and to the President, or to any official designated by the President, copies of its reports submitted to the party states pursuant to paragraph O of article IV of the compact.

fable.w: The Commission is an interstate compact body made up of party states, so it sits outside the federal government, and the section casts it as a consultative and recommendatory agency that cooperates with federal agencies and sends its reports to Congress and the President. That is coordination across the federal boundary through an advisory-type body. The opposite reading is tempting because the section mainly limits Congress's consent and names no specific federal decision, so this is a close call.
fable.s: the Commission shall be solely a consultative and recommendatory agency which will cooperate with the agencies of the United States

opus.w: The Commission is created by an interstate compact among the party states, so it is a non-federal body. The statute makes it a consultative and recommendatory body that cooperates with federal agencies, so outside parties advise and coordinate with the federal government. The tempting 'No' reading treats this as just a report to Congress or a limit on foreign cooperation. But the report goes from an outside body, and the consultative role toward U.S. agencies counts as participation across the federal boundary. The text does not name any specific federal decision the Commission advises on, which is why confidence is moderate.
opus.s: In carrying out its functions under this Act the Commission shall be solely a consultative and recommendatory agency which will cooperate with the agencies of the United States.
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** This looks like a "No" because the only clear process is the Commission sending reports to Congress and the President, which normally counts as a report to Congress. It also *restricts* the Commission's cooperation with foreign governments.

**Why that fails:** The Commission here is an interstate compact body made up of the member states, so it sits outside the federal government. The statute makes it a "consultative and recommendatory agency" that "will cooperate with the agencies of the United States." That means an outside entity advises and coordinates with federal agencies, which crosses the federal boundary. It is not like an agency's own report to Congress.

qwen_chat.w: The section defines the Commission's role as consultative and recommendatory, but restricts its cooperation to 'agencies of the United States' and its reporting to Congress and the President. Since all these entities are inside the federal government, there is no participation by outside parties as defined. The text explicitly excludes cooperation with foreign or international bodies, and does not mention states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: In carrying out its functions under this Act the Commission shall be solely a consultative and recommendatory agency which will cooperate with the agencies of the United States. It shall furnish to the Congress and to the President, or to any official designated by the President, copies of its reports submitted to the party states pursuant to paragraph O of article IV of the compact.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Commission is described as a "consultative and recommendatory agency," it inherently involves participation. However, the text explicitly limits its cooperation to "agencies of the United States" (inside the government) and its reporting to Congress and the President (inside the government). There is no mention of consulting with states, tribes, the public, or other outside entities. The definition states that consultation between federal agencies or officials is not participation.
